01 · OPEN

Orxan opens Booking.com.

The browser downloads the page. A nearby CDN can return images, JavaScript and CSS without contacting the application for every file.

Docker packages the app, runtime and dependencies. The same container image behaves consistently on a laptop, in testing and in production. Kubernetes runs and manages those containers.
Orxan enters booking.com
02 · ROUTE

Send him to a healthy region.

DNS and a global load balancer select a nearby healthy region. A region is a geographical cloud location containing data centres and clusters.

03 · RUN

A cluster runs the services.

The cluster is infrastructure: control plane plus worker nodes. Nodes provide CPU and RAM. Kubernetes places application Pods on them and restores the desired state.

Region → Kubernetes cluster → worker nodes → namespaces → Deployments → Pods. A Kubernetes Service gives changing Pods one stable address and balances traffic across ready replicas.

04 · SEARCH

Find available rooms.

The API Gateway checks identity and rate limits, then calls Search. Redis returns popular data quickly; PostgreSQL remains the source of truth.

Gateway → Kubernetes Service → ready Search Pod → Redis. On a miss: read a database replica, cache the result briefly, then return availability. Before booking, inventory is validated again.

05 · SCALE & RELEASE

Traffic changes. Features change.

Horizontal scaling adds Pods. Vertical scaling gives a Pod more CPU/RAM. A rolling deployment starts v2 gradually while healthy v1 Pods continue serving.

ConfigMaps hold non-secret configuration. Secrets hold credentials for authorised workloads. Feature flags target users or cohorts—not random Pods. Canary routing can send a small traffic percentage to v2.

06 · BOOK & PAY

Confirm once—even after failure.

Booking reserves inventory. Payment calls the provider with an idempotency key. Events go to workers through Kafka or RabbitMQ. Reconciliation repairs unknown outcomes.

Kafka: durable event stream, replay and many consumer groups. RabbitMQ: work queues, acknowledgements, routing and dead-letter queues. Retry temporary failures with timeout, backoff, jitter and a maximum attempt count.
READY · booking orx-7f21
Booking → Payment → external provider
Events → broker → email / analytics workers
Remember: Kubernetes keeps infrastructure close to declared state. Your application must still make business operations—especially payments—idempotent and recoverable.
